protocol.name: nidara_material_v1

description.summary: compositor-side materials for Nidara's glass

protocol.description: A surface declares the shapes of its glass and how the compositor resolves them against what lies behind: the blur's size and passes, per surface. The shapes are exact (rounded rectangles whose corners are superellipse quadrants, the shell's squircle), so the blur never depends on the alpha of the surface's own pixels: a low-alpha shadow next to the glass is not blurred because it is not in a shape.

request.name: get_material

description.summary: the material object of a surface

request.description: One per wl_surface; the state is double-buffered on wl_surface.commit.

description.summary: remove the material on the next commit

request.name: clear_shapes

description.summary: pending: no shapes (no material)

request.description: The ink boxes (add_ink_box) and veil regions (add_veil_region) go with them, the tones (set_tone, set_ink_tone) are reset to none, and the shapes' blur (set_shape_blur) to the surface's.

request.name: add_shape

description.summary: pending: add one glass shape

request.description: Surface-local, logical coordinates. corner_radius and exponent describe each corner: a superellipse quadrant of that radius (exponent 2 is a circular arc). Fixed-point values.

request.name: set_blur

description.summary: pending: blur size and passes for this surface

request.description: size is the kawase offset in logical pixels, passes the number of downsampling levels. passes 0 = no blur.

request.name: set_glass

description.summary: pending: the compositor paints the glass itself

request.description:
The compositor resolves the whole glass against the real backdrop, per pixel: the blurred backdrop, refracted near the edge; the tone of each shape (set_tone); and a specular rim. The client then paints only its content and state (active fills, hover), not the glass.
tint_r, tint_g, tint_b, alpha_min, alpha_max, target_luminance and saturation are inert: they drove a tint that thickened per pixel to keep content legible, which set_tone replaced. A shape with no tone is the blurred, refracted backdrop alone.

description.summary: pending: back to blur only; the client paints its glass

request.name: add_shape_clipped

description.summary: pending: add one glass shape, faded and clipped

request.description:
As add_shape, plus what a toolkit does to the widget that paints the glass. opacity is how FORMED the glass is in this shape, 0..1 — not a coverage: glass appearing materializes. The blur's reach, the refraction, the tint, the rim and the shadow under it all grow with it, so a panel appearing or going sends it every frame (add_shape is 1). The clip rectangle, in the same coordinates, is what of the shape may show: a card scrolled half out of its list is cut straight where the list ends, not rounded. A clip of zero width or height means no clip.
Shapes are drawn in the order they are added, a later one over an earlier one.

request.name: add_ink_box

description.summary: pending: where content of one ink group sits

request.description:
Surface-local, logical coordinates: a box where the client draws content (text, symbolic icons) whose colour it can switch, belonging to the ink group id (a number of the client's choosing, one per pane of glass). A group may have several boxes. Cleared by clear_shapes.
While set_ink is in force, the compositor measures the darkest point of the backdrop under each group's boxes, as the glass treats it (blurred and saturated, before its tint), and tells the client with the ink event when the group's content should turn dark: only when even that darkest point is brighter than dark_above, and back only when it falls below light_below. Never by an area's average.

request.name: set_ink

description.summary: pending: measure the ink boxes, with these thresholds

request.description: Thresholds are WCAG relative (linear) luminances, 0..1, with light_below below dark_above (the gap is the hysteresis). A shape that holds a group whose ink is dark takes its set_ink_tone. The tint is inert (it was the veil laid over such a shape before set_ink_tone).

description.summary: pending: no ink measurement; every group is light again

request.name: add_shape_pointed

description.summary: pending: add one glass shape with a pointer

request.description: As add_shape_clipped, plus a pointer spliced into one side: a triangle from the shape's edge (its base centred on base_x, base_y, pointer_width wide) to the tip at tip_x, tip_y, whose tip is a circular arc of tip_radius and which meets the shape's edge in a concave arc of base_radius. Body and pointer are one glass: one refraction, one rim. The coordinates are the shape's.

event.name: ink

description.summary: the content of an ink group should be dark, or light

event.description: Sent when a group's decision changes; a group starts light (white content), so the first event for a group is always dark = 1. A group no longer declared keeps its last decision, and so does the client.

request.name: set_lensing

description.summary: pending: the refraction grows with the shape

request.description: The edge displacement of each shape of the glass becomes the larger of set_glass's refraction and size_fraction times the shape's shorter side, so a large pane bends its backdrop more than a small control. 0 (the initial value) gives every shape set_glass's refraction. Meaningful only while the compositor paints the glass (set_glass).

request.name: set_scrim

description.summary: inert: the shadow under the glass is gone

request.description: It laid a shadow under the glass with what a per-pixel tint was missing to keep content legible; set_tone replaced that tint, and nothing is missing any more. Accepted and ignored. Fixed veils (add_veil_region) do not need it.

arg.name: region_edge
arg.summary: a region's shadow at its rim, as a fraction of its centre's (0..1)

request.name: add_scrim_region

description.summary: inert: the shadow under the glass is gone

request.description: Accepted and ignored, like set_scrim. A shape inside one is claimed by no veil region.

request.name: set_fusion

description.summary: pending: the shapes added from now on fuse into one silhouette

request.description: The shapes added after this request, until the next set_fusion, belong to fusion group `group` (a number of the client's choosing; 0 = none). The shapes of one group are drawn as ONE pane of glass: the smooth union of their outlines. Two of them closer than `spacing` (logical px) are joined by a bridge that grows as they approach and breaks as they part, and one refraction and one rim follow the whole silhouette. A shape fading out (its opacity) also withdraws from the union, so a bridge to it recedes as it goes. A shape with a pointer fuses with nothing. Reset to 0 by clear_shapes.

arg.name: spacing
arg.summary: logical px: closer than this, two shapes join

request.name: set_fusion_merge

description.summary: pending: how far the current fusion group becomes one shape

request.description: The fusion group set by the last set_fusion is drawn `merge` of the way (0..1) from the smooth union of its shapes towards their envelope: ONE shape spanning them all — the bounds of its shapes whose opacity is at least a half, with the smallest of their corner radii. At 1 the group is that one shape, refraction and rim included; on the way, the space between the shapes fills from their middle outwards, and the silhouette never goes past the envelope nor inside the union. Holds for the shapes added after it, until the next set_fusion or set_fusion_merge; reset to 0 by set_fusion and clear_shapes. Meaningless outside a fusion group.

request.name: set_drawn_region

description.summary: pending: the part of the surface its content is drawn in

request.description:
Surface-local, logical coordinates, like wl_surface.set_opaque_region: the compositor draws the surface's content (its buffer and its subsurfaces') only inside this region, and treats the rest as transparent without sampling it. For a surface far larger than what it paints — a layer the size of the monitor that holds a strip and a panel — so that what changes under it is not blended through its empty pixels. Content outside the region is NOT DRAWN. The glass (the shapes) is not affected: it is the compositor's own.
A null region, the initial state, is the whole surface. Not cleared by clear_shapes; destroying the material clears it. The region is copied when this request is received, so it may be destroyed at once.

request.name: add_veil_region

description.summary: pending: a FIXED veil under the shapes inside it

request.description:
Like add_scrim_region — surface-local, logical; every shape whose centre lies inside it is claimed by it — but what it casts is not measured: a black veil of opacity strength (0..1), even under the whole rectangle, falling to nothing over falloff logical pixels outside it as (1 − d/falloff)^exponent. It needs no set_scrim and the backdrop's brightness does not change it. It fades with the shapes' opacity. Cleared by clear_shapes; meaningful only while the compositor paints the glass (set_glass).
The darkening a group of panes lies on, behind them, rather than a shadow that makes up what the glass lacks.

arg.name: exponent
arg.summary: the fall-off's shape outside the rectangle: 1 linear, more falls faster near it

request.name: set_tone

description.summary: pending: the tone of the shapes added from now on

request.description:
How the glass treats the blurred backdrop under the shapes added after this request, until the next set_tone, in this order, on the sRGB-encoded colour:
1. saturation, about the Rec.709 luma (1 = unchanged); 2. ceiling: the luma l is brought to l·(1 − (1 − ceiling)·l), so white ends at ceiling and the mid tones bend towards it (1 = unchanged); 3. levels: lift + (gain − lift)·v, where black lands and where white would (0 and 1 = unchanged); 4. wash: the colour wash_r, wash_g, wash_b laid over at opacity wash_a (0 = none); 5. ambient: what surrounds the pane, blurred far wider than the glass (0.35 of the shape's shorter side), mapped by ambient_lift + (ambient_gain − ambient_lift)·w, lightens what is darker than it, at an opacity of ambient times how large the shape is — none for a shorter side up to 64 logical px, all of it from 160 (0 = none).
All of it grows with how formed the shape is. Reset to none (the backdrop as it is, blurred and refracted) by clear_shapes.

arg.name: ambient
arg.summary: 0..1, its opacity on a large shape

request.name: set_ink_tone

description.summary: pending: the tone of those shapes while their content is dark

request.description: The tone (as set_tone) a shape added after this request takes while its ink group's content is dark (set_ink). Until it is set — and after set_tone and clear_shapes, which reset it — a shape keeps its set_tone whatever its ink.

request.name: set_shape_blur

description.summary: pending: the blur of the shapes added from now on

request.description: The blur (as set_blur: the kawase offset in logical pixels and the number of passes) of the shapes added after this request, until the next set_shape_blur, in place of the surface's: a large pane is blurred further than the small controls beside it on the same surface, as the reference material blurs its menus and panels further than its buttons. passes 0 = the surface's blur (set_blur). Reset to it by clear_shapes.
